artifacts.title: The Toaster That Prints Notes From Your Future Self
artifacts.accessionNote: Recovered from the staff kitchen of the Municipal Bureau of Advance Notice.
artifacts.summary: A two-slot municipal toaster browns short messages onto each slice, written and signed by whoever you will be a year from now. Citizens were advised to read before buttering, and never to reply.
artifacts.artifactLabel: The browning dial is marked in weeks rather than shades. The crumb tray still holds three unread slices, each stamped with an official date of issue.
artifacts.visualDescription: A rounded chrome toaster sits on a folded tea towel. Two slices stand half-risen in its slots, darkened with small handwriting, and its browning dial is marked in weeks instead of shades.
artifacts.imageAlt: Blueprint drawing of a two-slot toaster with a browning dial marked in weeks, and a detail view of a slice of toast carrying a short handwritten note.

choices.label: Read the note while it is warm

artifacts.title: The Switchboard for Conversations That Ended Too Soon
artifacts.accessionNote: Removed intact from the night exchange at Counterfactual Relay Station Four.
artifacts.summary: An operator's switchboard once routed calls to conversations that had ended mid-sentence, reconnecting both parties at the exact word where they stopped. Operators wore two headsets and were trained never to finish anyone's sentence for them.
artifacts.artifactLabel: Nearly every jack is labelled with the last word spoken before a line went quiet: because, anyway, actually, wait. One cord is still plugged in, and its lamp has not gone out.
artifacts.visualDescription: A wooden operator's switchboard stands upright, its face covered in rows of brass jacks with tiny word labels, one left blank. Braided cords hang in loops below, and a small lamp glows beside the one connected cord.
artifacts.imageAlt: Blueprint drawing of an upright switchboard with rows of labelled jacks and looped cords, and a detail view of a single lit jack labelled WAIT.

choices.label: Answer the line that is still lit
Plug a cord into the blank jack

artifacts.title: The Kettle That Brews the Weather of Past Visits
artifacts.accessionNote: Donated by a lodging house that kept its guest book in steam instead of ink.
artifacts.summary: An enamel kettle records the weather outside each time a visitor was offered tea. When boiled, it releases a small cloud of that afternoon into the room, along with the smell of wet coats drying by the door.
artifacts.artifactLabel: The spout is lightly frosted, though the kettle has not been cold in years. Painted around the base are small tallies, one for every guest who stayed for a second cup.
artifacts.visualDescription: A pale blue enamel kettle sits on a cast-iron trivet. A thin curl of grey cloud hangs above its spout, faint frost rims the spout's edge, and rows of small painted tally marks circle its base.
artifacts.imageAlt: Blueprint drawing of a domed stovetop kettle on a trivet with a small cloud rising from its spout, and a detail view of tally marks painted around its base.

outcomes.title: The note is in your handwriting
outcomes.body: It says: Leave earlier on Thursday. Nothing else. The crumbs settle into a date three weeks from now, and the stamp on the crust reads Advice Issued, Not Binding.
outcomes.why: The note implies you will be arriving somewhere early on Thursday, and the kettle is where this museum keeps the weather of arriving at someone's door.

outcomes.title: The message goes under the butter
outcomes.body: The words soften and disappear. The toaster clicks once, politely, and raises a second slice that says only Understood. Somewhere ahead of you, a version of you stops drafting advice.
outcomes.why: Your future self now holds a message it never delivered, and the switchboard is where undelivered conversations wait to be connected.

outcomes.title: A sentence resumes mid-word
outcomes.body: A voice finishes saying because, then pauses, surprised that anyone is still there. It explains the rest in under a minute. It was not about you, and it was never as bad as it sounded.
outcomes.why: An old conversation has just ended kindly, and the umbrella keeps the shelter that conversations like it were once held under.

outcomes.title: The exchange goes quiet
outcomes.body: Two hundred conversations stop on the same word. In the silence, the operator's chair turns slightly toward you, and a card drops from the ledger: Service suspended at the caller's request.
outcomes.why: Silencing two hundred conversations leaves an unexpected gap in the afternoon, and the vending machine sells days to anyone holding a gap like that.

outcomes.title: The blank jack rings back
outcomes.body: The unlabelled jack connects to a conversation that has not happened yet. You hear yourself say anyway, someone laughs, and the line holds its breath, waiting for the rest.
outcomes.why: You have just overheard yourself in a future conversation, and the toaster is the exhibit that lets that future self leave you a note.

outcomes.title: An afternoon comes back indoors
outcomes.body: Steam gathers under the ceiling into a low, patient drizzle. A coat is drying by a door that is not there, and a voice asks whether you are staying for a second cup. You are counted.
outcomes.why: A question has been asked in a kitchen and left waiting for your answer, and the switchboard holds conversations that stopped before anyone replied.

outcomes.title: The kettle stays cold
outcomes.body: Nothing boils. For a while afterwards, your visitors arrive in perfectly ordinary weather and leave before the rain, and none of them can say later what the sky was doing while you talked.
outcomes.why: Conversations that leave no trace are the telephone's specialty; it connects callers to the talk they did not have.

rewire.why: A missed call from your own number, eleven years ahead, is followed naturally by the one exhibit that prints what your future self wanted to say.
A weekend kept intact is a weekend for visitors, and the kettle records the weather of every afternoon someone stayed for tea.
A voice calling everyone inside before the thunder never finished its sentence, and the switchboard reconnects sentences at the word where they stopped.

plateBriefs.figures: fig. 1 — three-quarter elevation of a rounded two-slot toaster, two slices half-risen, side lever and browning dial visible. fig. 2 — circled detail of one slice face-on, three short ruled lines of handwriting and a small square date stamp at the crust.
plateBriefs.motif: Dial ticks read 1 WK to 52 WK where shades would be; the slice in fig. 2 may carry class="slice" for a gentle rise later.

plateBriefs.figures: fig. 1 — front elevation of an upright operator's switchboard: grid of jacks, a shelf of cord plugs, three cords hanging in loops, one cord plugged in. fig. 2 — rounded-box detail of a single jack with its tiny word label (WAIT) and the lamp beside it.
plateBriefs.motif: Jack labels are single words (BECAUSE, ANYWAY, ACTUALLY, WAIT) with one left empty; the lit lamp may carry class="lamp" for a slow glow later.

plateBriefs.figures: fig. 1 — side elevation of a domed stovetop kettle on a three-legged trivet, a small outlined cloud rising from the spout. fig. 2 — circled detail of the base band showing rows of tally marks in groups of five.
plateBriefs.motif: The cloud is drawn in the same line weight as the kettle, as if it were part of the appliance; it may carry class="cloud" for a slow drift later.
